newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Brunel to be floated at NLG 41.00 per share.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Brunel to be floated at NLG 41.00 per share.

text.p: Shares in Dutch specialist temporary employment firm Brunel International will be floated on the Amsterdam Bourse at 41.00 guilders each, ABN AMRO Rothschild and Brunel said on Thursday.
ABN AMRO and Brunel previously said the shares were to be priced at 36 to 41 guilders per share.
Trading in Brunel is expected to start at about 1030 GMT today.
The flotation consists of 5.56 million existing Brunel shares and 1.95 million newly issued shares.
The banking syndicate has an option to buy an additional 1.13 million shares to cover over-allotments.

ABN AMRO Rothschild and Brunel said the flotation had been oversubscribed about 30 times, with hefty demand from both Dutch private investors and institutional investors in and outside the Netherlands.
Private buyers, Dutch and foreign institutional investors had each been awarded about one third of the number of shares available.
ABN AMRO Rothschild and Brunel said they had requested the members of the banking syndicate to allocate the shares to their clients as evenly as possible.

Brunel specialises in supplying highly trained temporary staff in information technology and engineering disciplines. The company posted 1996 net profit of 18.9 million guilders on turnover of 254.3 million. It previously said it expected substantial profit and turnover growth in 1997.
